rows.title: Budget watchdog warns the cost of Ottawa's borrowing goes beyond the deficit
rows.original_source: Parliamentary Budget Officer (PBO) via The Canadian Press
rows.provider: The Canadian Press (republished by the Penticton Herald)
rows.summary: Canada's Parliamentary Budget Officer, Annette Ryan, released her independent review of Budget 2026 on Nov. 17, concluding that the budget spends more, invests more and borrows more instead of spending less. New measures across the Carney government's three fiscal plans add up to $331.6 billion, and about 60% of that goes to day-to-day operations rather than capital investment. Higher oil prices and stronger revenues created $158.3 billion of new fiscal room over five years, but new measures of $151.5 billion used up 96% of it, so the 2026-27 deficit is projected at $62.3 billion instead of the $43.8 billion it would have been without them. Ottawa is expected to borrow $764.7 billion over five years, far more than the $289 billion in cumulative deficits, mainly because loans to Crown corporations and purchases like military equipment are borrowed now but only gradually show up in the deficit. Public debt charges are the fastest-growing item in the budget and are expected to overtake federal health transfers to the provinces, reaching about $2,000 per Canadian a year by 2030-31.
rows.fact: The PBO found $331.6 billion in new measures across three Carney-era plans and projects a 2026-27 deficit of $62.3 billion, with five-year borrowing of $764.7 billion. The deficit-based fiscal anchor has only about $2 billion of room in 2027-28.
rows.outlook: The PBO expects debt charges to keep climbing faster than any other spending line and to exceed health transfers to provinces in coming years.
rows.why: 정부가 갑자기 생긴 세수(재정 여력)를 저축하지 않고 거의 다 지출할 때 적자·국채·이자 비용이 어떻게 늘어나는지, 그리고 '적자'와 '실제 차입'이 왜 다른지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows what happens to deficits, debt and interest costs when a government spends almost all of a revenue windfall, and why the deficit and actual borrowing can be very different numbers.
rows.term_def: The extra money a government can spend (or the extra deficit it can avoid) without breaking its own budget plan, for example when tax revenue comes in higher than expected.
rows.note: Figures checked against the PBO's official Nov. 17, 2026 news release and a second free copy of the CP story (Investment Executive). This is the independent PBO review, a separate event from the finance minister's Nov. 12 budget defence covered earlier.

opinion.title: Carney government's three spending plans total $331.6 billion in new measures, budget watchdog finds
opinion.author: The Hub Staff
opinion.summary: This analysis argues that Ottawa spent nearly all of a revenue windfall, so the deficit shrinks only slightly while the real risks are thin margins under its fiscal anchors, heavy borrowing and rising debt charges. Drawing on economist Charles Lammam, it says banking the windfall would have cut five-year deficits to about $137 billion instead of $289 billion, and that net debt could rise from about 45% to 48% of GDP. Debt charges are projected to grow from $53.5 billion in 2025-26 to $85.5 billion in 2030-31, taking about 14 cents of every revenue dollar instead of 10. It notes that loans to Crown corporations and capital purchases sit outside the deficit but are still borrowed at interest. Citing economist Trevor Tombe, it concludes that whether the plan works depends on productivity growth recovering from its very weak pace.
opinion.why: 재정 적자와 국가 부채가 결국 '생산성'과 이자 부담에 달려 있다는 점을 숫자로 보여 주어, 정부 재정의 지속 가능성을 판단하는 방법을 익힐 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It uses concrete numbers to show that a government's fiscal sustainability ultimately depends on productivity growth and interest costs, teaching how to judge whether public finances add up.

rows.title: Retail spending slowed in October as high prices gave shoppers pause
rows.original_source: U.S. Commerce Department (Census Bureau) via The Associated Press
rows.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department reported on Nov. 17 that retail sales rose just 0.2% in October, down from a 0.8% gain in September. Gas station sales jumped 1.5%, so sales excluding gas stations grew only 0.1%, while car dealers fell 1.6% and furniture, clothing and sporting goods stores also declined. Because retail sales are not adjusted for inflation and consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, shoppers actually bought slightly less in real terms. The 'control group,' a core measure used to calculate GDP, still rose a solid 0.6%, helped by online sales that got a boost from an early-October Amazon Prime Day. The report is the last major spending reading before the holiday season, as retailers push low prices and credit card balances have reached $1.17 trillion.
rows.fact: Retail sales rose 0.2% in October after a 0.8% gain in September; excluding gas stations they rose only 0.1%, while the control group rose 0.6%. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in the same month, and credit card balances stood at $1.17 trillion, up 5.1% from a year earlier.
rows.outlook: Economists quoted by AP said middle- and moderate-income households are feeling the strain of higher prices and are turning more cautious heading into the holidays.
rows.why: 판매액(명목)이 늘어도 물가가 더 많이 오르면 실제 소비량(실질)은 줄어든다는 '명목 대 실질'의 차이를 미국 소비 데이터로 직접 확인할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It lets you see the difference between nominal and real numbers in action: sales grew in dollars, but prices rose faster, so Americans actually bought less.
rows.term_def: Nominal numbers are measured in today's dollars; real numbers remove the effect of price changes. If sales rise 0.2% but prices rise 0.4%, people really bought about 0.2% less stuff.
rows.note: Figures cross-checked with the original AP version (ABC News), Reuters and CNN reports of the same Nov. 17 release; the Census page itself could not be loaded.

opinion.title: US retail sales and manufacturing suggest strong momentum
opinion.author: James Knightley (Chief International Economist, US, ING)
opinion.summary: ING's chief US economist reads the same report more positively: the control group rose 0.6% against about 0.3% expected, and September was revised up to 0.5%. He agrees that after hot October inflation, headline sales fell in real terms and the control group was roughly flat, but says consumer spending should still add modestly to fourth-quarter growth. He describes spending as split by income: lower- and middle-income households' wages lag living costs, while wealthier households spend more, mostly on services and travel that retail sales do not capture. He also notes that industrial production fell 0.4% because mild weather cut utility output, while manufacturing itself rose 0.3% and the ISM factory index climbed to 55.5. Overall, he sees underlying momentum consistent with roughly 2.5% GDP growth.
opinion.why: 같은 지표를 두고도 전문가들이 '소비 위축'과 '견조한 성장'으로 다르게 해석하는 이유, 그리고 소득 계층별로 소비가 갈리는 'K자형' 경제를 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows why experts can read the same data as either weakness or strength, and explains how spending splits between higher- and lower-income households.

rows.title: Household credit growth slows in Q3 amid high market rate
rows.original_source: Bank of Korea preliminary data via Yonhap News Agency
rows.summary: The Bank of Korea reported on Nov. 18 that South Korea's household credit (household loans plus unpaid card purchases) reached a record 2,030.5 trillion won at the end of September. It rose 9.8 trillion won from the previous quarter, the smallest increase in about a year and a half and far below the second quarter's 26.4 trillion won gain. Household loans grew only 4.7 trillion won to 1,896.8 trillion won, as non-mortgage loans, including stock margin lending, fell 4.9 trillion won while mortgage loans climbed to a record 1,202.3 trillion won. The slowdown came as interest rates stayed high: the BOK raised its base rate in July and August as a preemptive move against inflation and held it at 3% in October. Slower borrowing matters because Korea's household debt is very large relative to its economy, which makes families sensitive to higher interest rates.
rows.fact: Household credit hit a record 2,030.5 trillion won at end-September, up 9.8 trillion won on the quarter versus 26.4 trillion won in Q2. Non-mortgage loans fell 4.9 trillion won, while mortgage balances rose to a record 1,202.3 trillion won.
rows.outlook: A BOK official expects the household debt-to-GDP ratio to have fallen in Q3, though home prices, apartment move-ins and stock market swings could change the trend.
rows.why: 금리 인상과 주식시장 조정이 가계 대출에 어떤 영향을 주는지, 그리고 가계 부채가 경제 전체에서 왜 중요한 위험 요인인지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how higher interest rates and a stock market correction affect household borrowing, and why household debt is a key risk for the whole economy.
rows.term_def: All the money households owe divided by the size of the whole economy (GDP). If debt grows more slowly than the economy, the ratio falls, meaning the debt burden is getting lighter.
rows.note: Core figures (2,030.5T, +9.8T, 1,896.8T, +4.7T, -4.9T, 1,202.3T won) match Seoul Economic Daily and AJU Press reports of the same BOK release. Sources differ on the size of the mortgage increase, so only the mortgage level is used.

opinion.title: Korea's household debt grows by slowest in six quaters
opinion.author: Kim Yeon-jae
opinion.summary: This analysis, based on a BOK briefing, explains what drove the slowdown. According to the BOK's financial statistics team, non-mortgage loans fell mainly because the stock market corrected and investors paid back margin loans, not because of higher interest rates. Housing loans slowed as home sales dropped, mostly through group loans for new apartment projects, while individual mortgages barely slowed. Card purchase debt jumped 5 trillion won, which the BOK linked to installment and cashback promotions rather than a real rebound in consumption, since private spending fell in the quarter. The piece notes that the debt-to-GDP ratio is close to falling below 80%, and that slower borrowing may ease pressure on the BOK before its final 2026 rate meeting on Nov. 26.
opinion.why: 부채 증가가 둔화된 진짜 원인(금리인지, 주식시장인지, 주택 거래인지)을 나눠서 살펴보며 경제 데이터를 해석하는 방법을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It breaks down the real causes behind slower borrowing (interest rates, stocks or home sales), teaching how to interpret economic data carefully.

rows.title: UK inflation rises to one-year high but markets trim rate hike bets
rows.original_source: Office for National Statistics (ONS) via Reuters
rows.summary: Britain's Office for National Statistics reported on Nov. 18 that consumer price inflation rose to 3.6% in the year to October from 3.5% in September, the highest in a year. The figure matched economists' forecasts but came in just below the Bank of England's own 3.7% projection, while core inflation held at 2.8% and services inflation stayed at 3.7%. The ONS said the rise was driven mainly by higher fuel prices and earlier-than-usual tobacco tax increases, while food price inflation slowed to 0.9%, the smallest rise since 2021. Much of the pressure is imported energy inflation linked to Middle East conflict, with motor fuel prices up sharply from a year earlier. After the data, investors lowered their bets on another Bank of England rate rise in December to about 80% from 90%, following its increase to 4% earlier this month.
rows.fact: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%, with core inflation steady at 2.8% and services at 3.7%. Fuel prices and tobacco taxes pushed prices up, while food inflation eased to 0.9%.
rows.outlook: The Bank of England forecasts inflation close to 5% in the second quarter of 2027, as regulated household energy bills are due to rise about 20% in January.
rows.why: 에너지 가격 같은 해외 요인으로 생긴 '수입 인플레이션'과 기조적인 '근원 인플레이션'을 구별해야 중앙은행의 금리 결정을 이해할 수 있다는 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It explains why central banks separate imported energy inflation from underlying core inflation when deciding interest rates.
rows.term_def: Inflation measured without the most jumpy prices such as energy, food, alcohol and tobacco. It shows the underlying trend in prices more clearly than the headline number.
rows.note: Reuters figures confirmed in a second free copy (RTE) and against Investing.com and Euronews reports of the same release; the ONS bulletin itself could not be loaded.

opinion.title: Inflation in October and energy bill estimates for January both driven by high wholesale gas prices: comment
opinion.author: Chris Jaccarini (Senior Economist, ECIU)
opinion.summary: ECIU economist Chris Jaccarini argues that high wholesale oil and gas prices, pushed up by the Middle East conflict, were the main force behind October's 3.6% inflation. He warns the same gas prices point to a sharp rise in household energy bills from January 2027, with earlier industry estimates of more than £250 a year. He says volatile fossil-fuel markets raise costs for heating, electricity, fuel and mortgages, and that higher inflation and borrowing costs have also shrunk the government's fiscal headroom. He criticises recent moves to weaken programs that help households switch away from oil and gas, such as cuts to the Boiler Upgrade Scheme. ECIU is a clean-energy think tank, so the piece argues for a policy position: more wind power and electrification to shield bills from gas price shocks.
opinion.why: 에너지 수입 의존이 물가·금리·정부 재정에까지 연쇄적으로 영향을 주는 과정과, 에너지 정책이 거시경제 정책이 될 수 있다는 관점을 접할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It traces how dependence on imported energy ripples into prices, interest rates and government finances, and presents the view that energy policy is also economic policy.

rows.title: Japan exports set record in October on strong chip-related demand
rows.original_source: Japan Ministry of Finance trade data via Reuters
rows.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance reported on Nov. 18 that exports rose 20.5% from a year earlier in October to a record of about 11.8 trillion yen, the 14th straight month of growth. Shipments to the United States rose 23.9% and to China 13.3%, as global investment in artificial intelligence boosted demand for Japanese chips and chipmaking equipment. Imports also hit a record, rising 21.6% to about 12.2 trillion yen, largely because crude oil became more expensive amid Middle East instability. That left a trade deficit of 476.5 billion yen, about half of what markets expected. Export volumes grew far less than export values, which suggests much of the jump came from higher prices, including companies passing rising costs on to customers.
rows.fact: October exports rose 20.5% year on year to a record of about 11.8 trillion yen, and imports rose 21.6% to a record of about 12.2 trillion yen. The trade deficit was 476.5 billion yen, smaller than the roughly 956 billion yen expected.
rows.outlook: Analysts said AI-related demand for chips and equipment should keep supporting exports, offsetting weak demand from China.
rows.why: AI 붐 같은 세계적 수요 변화가 한 나라의 수출을 어떻게 끌어올리는지, 그리고 수출이 늘어도 유가 상승 때문에 무역적자가 날 수 있는 이유를 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a global trend like the AI boom lifts a country's exports, and why a country can still run a trade deficit when oil import costs rise.
rows.term_def: When a country spends more on imports than it earns from exports over a period. Rising oil prices can create a deficit even when exports are growing strongly.
rows.note: Headline figures confirmed against Xinhua's Nov. 18, 2026 report of the same Ministry of Finance data (small differences are rounding).

opinion.title: Japan Trade Deficit Narrows as Chip Exports Surge, but Oil Costs Stay High
opinion.author: ActionForex staff
opinion.summary: This market commentary digs into the details behind the narrower deficit. Exports of chips and of chipmaking equipment each jumped about 50%, and car shipments to the U.S. rose strongly while those to China fell by more than half. On the import side, crude oil spending rose about 60% by value even though volume slightly fell, showing that higher prices, not more demand, drove the bill. It notes Japan is shifting oil purchases toward the United States as Middle East supply becomes riskier, and that a weaker yen, about 5.6% lower than a year earlier, made energy imports even more expensive. Citing NLI Research economist Taro Saito, it concludes that the smaller deficit reflects strong exports rather than easing import costs, so Japan remains exposed to oil price shocks.
opinion.why: 환율 약세와 유가 상승이 수입 비용을 어떻게 키우는지, 그리고 '금액'과 '물량'을 나눠 보아야 무역 통계를 제대로 읽을 수 있다는 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how a weak currency and high oil prices raise import costs, and why you must separate value from volume to read trade data correctly.
